mainTopic: Animals blemished before consecration: redeeming their offspring, רבי אלעזר's במת יחיד derivation, תמורה, and redemption after death
overview: The גמרא asks whether the offspring of an animal with only קדושת דמים can be redeemed while still unblemished. A ברייתא says yes, because the offspring (טפל) cannot be holier than its mother (עיקר); from this reasoning the גמרא supports רבא, who says an unblemished male consecrated 'for its value' gets קדושת הגוף. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's ruling that slaughtering such animals outside is פטור. רבי אלעזר reads it as חייב, about offering a blemished animal on a במת יחיד, and learns this through 'אם אינו ענין' from the verse 'לא תזבח' in דברים. The גמרא tests his derivation by proposing other uses for that verse: בכור, מעשר, תמורה, and ולדות קדשים. Each one turns out to have its own source, so רבי אלעזר's reading stands. Next, the גמרא learns from the verse 'a good for a bad' that an animal blemished before consecration cannot make a תמורה. Finally, רב says the משנה's rule that such animals may be redeemed after death follows רבי שמעון, who excludes them from העמדה והערכה because of the word 'אותה'. The חכמים, identified as the תנא דבי לוי, require burial, and the גמרא begins to ask why רב limited the משנה to רבי שמעון, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can the offspring be redeemed while unblemished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the offspring of an animal with only קדושת דמים can be redeemed while still unblemished, or whether one must wait for it to get a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they redeemed while unblemished, or are they not redeemed while unblemished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the babies of animals that were holy only for their money value: can we redeem them right away, or must we wait until they get a blemish?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal with קדושת הגוף passes that body-holiness to its offspring, so the offspring cannot be redeemed until it is blemished. Here the mother has only קדושת דמים. The question is whether the offspring is treated like the mother, and can be redeemed now, or whether it is treated more strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: are redeemed (exchanged for money, which removes their holiness)
unblemished, physically whole animals
holiness of value only: the animal is holy for its money value, not as a sacrifice
offspring

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'they' and 'unblemished' refer to the offspring, not the mother. The mother was blemished, so it only had קדושת דמים. The question is about her healthy, unblemished babies.

phrases.notes: Can the offspring be redeemed right away, with no blemish?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the offspring may be sold without a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that offspring of permanently blemished animals dedicated to the מזבח may be sold without a blemish, because the secondary item (טפל) cannot be stricter than the primary (עיקר).
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who dedicates permanently blemished animals for the altar, and they gave birth: the offspring may be sold, and they do not need a blemish. This is because holiness does not take effect on them, so that the secondary should not be stricter than the primary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question: the babies of blemished animals dedicated to the מזבח can be sold right away, with no blemish needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother was permanently blemished, so she could never become a real sacrifice and got only קדושת דמים. Her offspring draws its holiness from her. It would make no sense for the baby (טפל) to be holier than its mother (עיקר), so the baby also gets no קדושת הגוף and can be redeemed even while unblemished. This answers the question in step 1: נפדין תמימים.

one who dedicates (attaches holiness to an animal)
permanent blemishes

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule שלא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר is a general principle: something that draws its status from a source cannot have a stricter status than that source.

steps.title: Inference: an unblemished male consecrated for its value gets body-holiness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא's reasoning that holiness was blocked only because of טפל and עיקר. So an unblemished male consecrated directly 'for its value' does receive קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is so that the secondary should not be stricter than the primary. But if one consecrated a male for its value, it is holy with body-holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the ברייתא's reason and draws a new rule from it about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have said simply that consecrating 'for value' never creates body-holiness. Instead, it gave the special reason of טפל and עיקר. This implies that without that special reason, holiness would take hold. So when someone directly consecrates an unblemished male, which is fit to be offered, 'for its value', it becomes holy with קדושת הגוף.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is (introduces an inference from a stated reason)
he consecrated a male animal for its value
body-holiness: the animal itself becomes a sacrifice

steps.confusionAlert: This new case has no mother-and-offspring relationship. The male is itself the עיקר, and it is unblemished, so the טפל-and-עיקר limit does not apply to it.

phrases.english: The reason is so that the secondary should not be

steps.title: This inference supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this inference supports רבא, who ruled that a male consecrated for its value is holy with קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבא, as רבא said: If one consecrated a male for its value, it is holy with body-holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the rule it just inferred matches a known statement of רבא, so the ברייתא backs him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling is that the person's intent to consecrate only the value 'spreads' to the animal's body, because the animal is fit for the מזבח. The ברייתא's reasoning, read carefully, implies exactly this. So the ברייתא serves as support for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: supports him: this source backs up a known opinion
a leading אמורא of Babylonia

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring of an animal with only קדושת דמים may be redeemed unblemished, because the טפל cannot be stricter than the עיקר. An unblemished male consecrated directly for its value gets קדושת הגוף, as רבא ruled.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: slaughtering them outside is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one who slaughters these animals, whose blemish came before their consecration, outside the Temple is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes it. This sets up the next step, which reports a different reading of this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of שחוטי חוץ (slaughtering a sacrifice outside the Temple) applies only to an animal fit to be offered inside. These animals were blemished before they were consecrated and were never fit for the מזבח, so slaughtering them outside carries no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard
exempt from punishment
the prohibition of slaughtering sacrifices outside the Temple

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about animals blemished before consecration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section: the גמרא returns to the משנה to discuss another of its rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering animals blemished before their consecration outside the Temple carries no liability.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר reads 'liable' and places the case at a private altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches the משנה as 'חייב' and explains that it refers to offering on a private altar (במת יחיד).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר teaches it as 'liable', and he sets the case at a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different version of the משנה's text from רבי אלעזר, along with how he explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אלעזר's version, the liability is not for שחוטי חוץ. His case is the period when private altars (במות) were permitted. Offering a blemished animal on such a private altar breaks the prohibition against offering a בעל מום, so the person is liable to lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches (reads the text of a משנה in a certain way)
liable to punishment
he sets it in (applies the text to a specific case)
a private altar of an individual, permitted in certain periods

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר does not disagree that slaughtering outside the Temple is exempt from כרת. He reads 'liable' about a different situation: offering a blemished animal on a private altar.
steps.whatToRemember: First reading: slaughtering these animals outside is פטור, since they were never fit for the מזבח. רבי אלעזר's reading: חייב, in the case of a במת יחיד, for offering a בעל מום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar teaches 'liable',
phrases.notes: A different text of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative reading of the משנה line quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה reads 'חייב', referring to offering a blemished animal on a private altar.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's verse for a blemished animal on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a verse showing that offering a blemished animal on a במת יחיד, when private altars were allowed, breaks a לא תעשה. The verse in דברים is extra for the main altar, so it is applied to the private altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר said: How do we know that someone who offers a blemished animal on a private altar, at a time when private altars were allowed, breaks a negative commandment? Because the Torah says: 'Do not sacrifice to ה׳ your God an ox or a sheep [that has a blemish].' This verse is not needed for the big public altar, since that is already taught by 'blind or broken…'. So apply it to the private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי אלעזר's reading of the משנה as 'חייב' comes from. It is his own teaching that a verse forbids blemished animals even on a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two verses that forbid blemished animals. One is in ויקרא ('עורת או שבור') and the other is in דברים ('לא תזבח'). The ויקרא verse already covers the main Temple altar, so the דברים verse would be extra. רבי אלעזר uses the rule of 'אם אינו ענין' to send the extra verse to a new case, the במת יחיד. That is why someone who offers such an animal there is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar that an individual could build in certain periods of history
A time when private altars were allowed
The great public altar, like the one in the משכן or the בית המקדש
A negative commandment (a לאו)
'If it is not needed for its own topic…', a rule that moves an extra verse to a different case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the verse 'לא תזבח' is teaching the basic rule about the Temple altar. That rule is already known from ויקרא. Because this verse would otherwise be extra, it is used for the private altar.
steps.whyThisMatters: This derivation is what allows רבי אלעזר to read the משנה as 'חייב'. The rest of this passage tests whether the extra verse really belongs to the private altar.

steps.title: Why not apply the extra verse to a blemished firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the derivation. Maybe the extra verse should go to a בכור, which becomes holy even when blemished. The verse would then teach that a blemished בכור may not be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: if the verse is not needed for regular sacrifices, apply it to a firstborn animal. You might have thought that since a firstborn is holy even when it is blemished, it may also be offered when it is blemished. The verse would teach us that it may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the extra verse must go to the private altar. Perhaps it should go to a different case, the blemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is unusual because it becomes holy even if it was born blemished. So someone could have thought it may also be brought on the מזבח in that state. If the extra verse is needed to block that idea, then it is not available for רבי אלעזר's private-altar teaching.

A firstborn male animal, holy from birth
An animal with a blemish

steps.kashyaTarget: The application of דברים יז:א to a במת יחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra verse could just as well be needed for a blemished בכור. So it may not be free to teach the private-altar law.

steps.title: The firstborn already has its own verse
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that a blemished בכור is already forbidden by an explicit verse. So the extra verse is not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: about a firstborn, it is written openly: 'lame or blind, you shall not sacrifice it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the בכור suggestion. The Torah already says directly that a blemished בכור may not be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דברים טו:כא explicitly forbids offering a blemished בכור. The verse in דברים יז:א would add nothing for the בכור. So the extra verse is still free for רבי אלעזר's private altar.

steps.title: Why not apply the extra verse to a blemished animal tithe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Maybe the extra verse should go to מעשר בהמה, which is holy even when blemished. The verse would then teach that a blemished מעשר may not be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: if the verse is not needed for regular sacrifices, apply it to the animal tithe. You might have thought that since the tithe is holy even with its blemish, as it says 'he shall not check between good and bad', it may also be offered with its blemish. The verse would teach us that it may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another case that could use up the extra verse: the animal tithe. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מעשר בהמה, the owner may not pick out good or bad animals. Every tenth animal becomes holy, even a blemished one. So someone might think it can also be offered while blemished. Unlike בכור, no explicit verse has yet been shown for מעשר, so this challenge is stronger than the last one.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal becomes holy
'He shall not check between good and bad', so even a blemished tenth animal becomes holy
Since, because

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר, like בכור, becomes holy even when blemished, but it has no explicit verse yet. So the extra verse may be needed for it, leaving nothing for the private altar.

steps.title: Animal tithe is learned from firstborn through a shared word
steps.stepSummary: The verse is not needed for מעשר בהמה, because מעשר is linked to בכור through the shared word 'העברה'. A blemished בכור may not be offered, so a blemished מעשר may not be offered either.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: מעשר is also covered. It is learned from בכור, because the word 'passing' appears by both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. The extra verse is not needed for מעשר, because מעשר already gets its rule from בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both בכור and מעשר use the word 'העברה' (passing). This shared word lets us copy rules from one to the other. In Step 9 we saw that a verse explicitly forbids offering a blemished בכור, so the same rule moves over to מעשר. The verse in דברים is therefore still free to teach about a במת יחיד.

steps.title: Maybe the verse is about a substitute animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new use for the extra verse: תמורה. A תמורה becomes holy even if it is blemished, so we might think it can be offered while blemished. The verse would come to forbid that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that the verse teaches about a substitute for a sacrificial animal. You might have thought: since a substitute becomes holy even when it has a blemish (as it says 'He shall not exchange it nor substitute it'), it may also be offered with a blemish. The verse teaches that it may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another challenge. Maybe the extra verse is about תמורה and not about a במת יחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about תמורה says a bad animal swapped for a good one becomes holy, so even a blemished animal becomes holy as a תמורה. That makes it look different from normal offerings, so we might think it can also be brought on the מזבח. The extra verse could be needed to block that idea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מעשר is ruled out, the גמרא proposes a new case, תמורה, for the extra verse
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim (Step 7) that the extra verse must refer to a במת יחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If another case (תמורה) needs the verse, then the verse is not free to teach about a במת יחיד

steps.title: A substitute is compared to the original animal
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'הוא ותמורתו' compares the תמורה to the original קרבן. A blemished original cannot be offered, so a blemished תמורה cannot be offered either. The extra verse is not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'it and its substitute'. It compares the substitute to the original. Just as the original may not be offered with a blemish, so too its substitute may not be offered with a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the תמורה challenge. A different verse already teaches that a blemished תמורה cannot be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By putting the two side by side ('it and its substitute'), the תורה makes them equal. This is called a הקש. The original קרבן cannot be offered blemished, so the תמורה cannot either. The verse in דברים is still free for a במת יחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse says', brings a verse as the source
Compares, makes a הקש that gives two things the same law
'It and its substitute', the phrase that links them

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And it and its substitute shall be',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:י

phrases.english: it compares its substitute to it:
just as it may not be offered when blemished,
so too its substitute may not be offered when blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תמורה challenge from Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the proposed case already has a source (a הקש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra verse might be needed to forbid offering a blemished תמורה
steps.terutzMaskana: The הקש 'הוא ותמורתו' already forbids it, so the verse is not needed for תמורה

steps.title: רבי זירא: maybe the verse is about offspring of sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests the extra verse might be about ולדות קדשים. They are holy even when blemished because of their mother, so we might think they can be offered blemished. The verse would come to forbid that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Say the verse teaches about the offspring of sacrificial animals. You might have thought: since they are holy even when blemished because of their mother, they may also be offered when blemished. The verse teaches that they may not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא raises a new challenge to רבי אלעזר. Maybe the extra verse is about ולדות קדשים and not about a במת יחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby born to a sacrificial animal becomes holy automatically through its mother, even if it is born with a blemish. Because of that unusual holiness, we might think it can go on the מזבח while blemished. If the verse is needed to block this, then it is not free to teach about a במת יחיד. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Objects to it', a sage raises a strong challenge
An אמורא who raises the challenge here
Offspring born to sacrificial animals
'On account of their mother', their holiness comes from the mother
They are offered (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to it:
Say: apply it to the topic of offspring of sacrificial animals,
since it might enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּקְדוֹשִׁין כְּשֶׁהֵן בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אַגַּב אִמָּן,
phrases.english: since they are holy when they are blemished, on account of their mother,
they may also be offered when they are blemished,
so it teaches us that they may not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After תמורה is ruled out, רבי זירא proposes another case, ולדות קדשים, for the extra verse
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim (Step 7) that the extra verse must refer to a במת יחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ולדות קדשים gain holiness through their mother even when blemished, so the verse may be needed for them and not for a במת יחיד
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the same pattern: each candidate case must be shown to have its own source, or רבי אלעזר's reading of the verse falls.

steps.title: רבא: the school of רבי ישמעאל already settled this
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רבי זירא. The rule that blemished ולדות may not be offered is already taught by a ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל, so the extra verse is not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל already ruled on this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רבי זירא's idea that the extra verse is about ולדות קדשים. He says another source already covers that case, and the next step will quote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא wanted the extra verse to teach that blemished offspring may not be offered. רבא says that rule is already known from a different teaching. So the verse in דברים is still free to teach about a במת יחיד, and רבי אלעזר's derivation in Step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled it, he already settled it
The teacher of the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Rava says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael has already ruled it,
phrases.notes: He ruled that blemished offspring may not be offered, using a different verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's suggestion in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An existing source already covers the case, so the extra verse is not needed for it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra verse is needed to forbid offering blemished ולדות קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blemished ולדות are already forbidden through the ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: The verse links substitutes and offspring to a vowed offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'רק קדשיך' as the תמורות and 'אשר יהיו לך' as the ולדות. The word 'ונדריך' compares both of them to a נדר, which may not be offered blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'Only your holy things that you have, and your vows.' 'Only your holy things' means the substitutes. 'That you have' means the offspring. 'And your vows' means the verse compared them to a vowed offering. Just as a vowed offering may not be offered if blemished, these also may not be offered if blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that proves רבא's point. Each phrase of the verse is matched to a type of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the verse is read as one category: the תמורות, the ולדות, and the vowed offerings. Because they appear together in one verse, they are compared to each other (a היקש). A blemished vowed animal can never go on the altar, so blemished ולדות and תמורות cannot either.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute animals that became holy when someone swapped them for a קרבן
Offspring born to a consecrated animal
It compared them, a היקש (a comparison made because things appear together in a verse)
An offering someone obligated himself to bring by a vow

steps.whatToRemember: Blemished ולדות and תמורות may not be offered, because 'ונדריך' compares them to a vowed offering. Every proposed alternative (בכור, מעשר, תמורה, ולדות) already has its own source, so 'לא תזבח' in דברים יז:א stays with the במת יחיד, as רבי אלעזר taught.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Only your sacred items which you have, and your vows" —
phrases.notes: דברים יב:כו

phrases.english: "Only your sacred items": these are the substitutes,
"Which you have": these are the offspring,
"And your vows": the verse compared them to a vowed offering,
Just as a vowed offering is not offered when blemished,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָנֵי נָמֵי בַּעַל מוּם לֹא.
phrases.english: So too, these also are not offered when blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's claim in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That blemished ולדות and תמורות may not be offered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל on דברים יב:כו, comparing them to a נדר.

steps.title: Why can't an animal blemished from the start make a substitute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next ruling in the משנה, that such animals do not make a תמורה, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they do not make a substitute.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that an animal that was blemished before it was consecrated cannot make a תמורה. Normally, swapping a regular animal for a consecrated one makes the regular animal holy too. The גמרא wants to know why this animal is different.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not make a substitute holy
What is the reason?

phrases.english: "And they do not render a substitute" (quoting the משנה),
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that an animal blemished from the start does not make a תמורה.

steps.title: The source is the verse 'He shall not exchange it'
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from the verse 'לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר' about the laws of תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says: 'He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the verse that is the source. The next steps explain how the rule is read out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions 'good' and 'bad' animals in a swap. The exact lesson comes from noticing that one half of the verse seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not exchange it nor substitute it (ויקרא כז:י)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: As the verse states: "He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, etc."
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'a good for a bad, or a bad for a good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse ויקרא כז:י, which speaks of 'good' and 'bad' animals.

steps.title: One half of the verse seems unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: If even swapping a bad animal for a good one is forbidden, there should be no need to say that swapping a good animal for a bad one is forbidden. So why does the verse say both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since you said a bad one for a good one is not allowed, is it necessary to say a good one for a bad one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one half of the verse looks unneeded. It is setting up a new reading of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding the 'easier' swap automatically forbids the 'obvious' one. So the phrase 'good for bad' must be teaching something else. The next step explains what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (since we already know this)
Is it necessary to say?

phrases.english: Now that you have said a bad one for a good one is not allowed,
is it necessary to say a good one for a bad one?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא רַע בְּטוֹב אָמְרַתְּ לֹא, טוֹב בְּרָע מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the verse cited in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of 'טוב ברע או רע בטוב' as two separate prohibitions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One half is already implied by the other, so the verse looks redundant.

steps.title: Only an animal good from the outset makes a substitute
steps.stepSummary: The 'extra' wording teaches a new rule. An animal that was unblemished when consecrated makes a תמורה. An animal that was blemished before consecration does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, an animal that was good from the start makes a substitute holy. An animal that was bad from the start does not make a substitute holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The extra words teach the rule of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Good' and 'bad' are now read as the condition of the original animal at the moment it was consecrated. Only an animal that was fit when consecrated can pass holiness on to a substitute. This is the source for the משנה's rule from Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outset, from the beginning
An animal that was blemished before it was consecrated

steps.whatToRemember: An animal blemished before it was consecrated cannot make a תמורה. This is learned from the seemingly extra 'good/bad' wording in the verse.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'good' and 'bad' do not describe the animals in the swap as such. They describe the original consecrated animal's condition at the moment it became holy.

phrases.english: Rather, an animal good at the outset renders a substitute holy,
but an animal bad at the outset does not render a substitute holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the redundancy raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the redundant wording to teach a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse simply forbids both kinds of swaps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that only an animal unblemished when consecrated can make a תמורה.

steps.title: רב: redeeming after death follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says these animals may be redeemed even after they die. רב says this follows רבי שמעון. In his view, only altar-sanctified animals need העמדה והערכה; items for בדק הבית do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If they died, they may be redeemed.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי שמעון, who said: Animals consecrated for the altar were included in the requirement of standing and valuation. Items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included in standing and valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ruling from the משנה and tells us whose opinion it follows. It explains why a dead animal could still be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem some consecrated animals, they must be stood before a כהן to be valued (העמדה והערכה). A dead animal cannot be stood up, so it cannot be redeemed that way. רבי שמעון limits this requirement to animals with altar holiness, so items without that holiness can be redeemed even after death.

keyTerms.meaning: If they died, they may be redeemed
Standing the animal before a כהן and having him value it
Things consecrated to be offered on the altar
Things consecrated for Temple maintenance (their value goes to the Temple)

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the practical result that a dead animal that was blemished from the start can still be redeemed, and it ties the משנה to רבי שמעון's view.

phrases.english: "If they died, they may be redeemed" (quoting the משנה).
Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who says:

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: Items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation,

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.
phrases.english: items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included in standing and valuation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling that these animals may be redeemed after death follows רבי שמעון. He requires העמדה והערכה only for altar-sanctified animals.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's view from the משנה in תמורה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבי שמעון allows items for בדק הבית to be redeemed after death. He also agrees that an animal blemished from the outset may be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי שמעון says: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died, may be redeemed. And רבי שמעון agrees that an animal blemished from the start may be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב's statement about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Items for בדק הבית may be redeemed after death because they do not need העמדה. רבי שמעון also concedes that an animal blemished before consecration, even if it was dedicated to the altar, may be redeemed after death. That is exactly the case in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees, concedes
An animal blemished from the outset, before it was consecrated

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: תמורה לב.

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, אִם מֵתוּ — יִפָּדוּ.
phrases.english: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died, may be redeemed.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁנִּפְדֶּה.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding an animal blemished from the outset that it may be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's attribution in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's ruling about redeeming after death matches רבי שמעון's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תמורה quoting רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Why does an animal blemished from the start not need valuation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי שמעון's concession about an animal blemished from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון agrees in this case. It sets up the verse that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an animal was dedicated to the altar, and altar animals normally need העמדה והערכה. So the גמרא wants to know why this one is an exception.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the concession in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that excludes an animal blemished from the outset from העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: The word 'it' excludes an animal blemished from the outset
steps.stepSummary: The verses about העמדה והערכה say 'אותה' ('it'). This limits the requirement and excludes an animal that was blemished before it was consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says 'it' and 'it', to exclude an animal blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a word in the verse that limits the rule. This explains רבי שמעון's concession. The quoted משנה then continues with the חכמים' opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אותה' in ויקרא כז:יא–יב narrows who needs העמדה והערכה. An animal blemished from the start never had full altar holiness, so it is left out. Since it does not need to be stood up, it can be redeemed even after it dies.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It', a word read as limiting the rule
To exclude

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, an animal blemished before consecration does not need העמדה והערכה, because of the word 'אותה'. So it can be redeemed even after death.

phrases.english: As the verse states: "it," "it" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:יא–יב: 'he shall stand it... the priest shall appraise it'

phrases.english: to exclude an animal blemished from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limiting word 'אותה' excludes an animal blemished from the outset from העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: The Sages say dead consecrated animals are buried
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends with the חכמים: if consecrated animals die, they must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Sages say: if they died, they must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in תמורה that it began earlier. The חכמים argue with רבי שמעון and say that animals which died may not be redeemed. They must be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that animals for בדק הבית can be redeemed even after death. The חכמים say all of them, including those for בדק הבית, must be buried. Their reason is that every animal needs העמדה והערכה, and a dead animal cannot be stood up and valued.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, meaning the majority opinion
They must be buried

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
If they died, they must be buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 22 by giving the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, consecrated animals that died must be buried and cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: Who are these Sages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the Sages?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which specific תנא stands behind the חכמים' opinion. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that even רבי שמעון agrees that an animal blemished before consecration can be redeemed, because of 'אותה'. So the גמרא wants to know who would say that every dead animal is buried, with no exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים quoted in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who says all dead consecrated animals must be buried.

steps.title: The Sages are the school of לוי
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are the תנא דבי לוי, who includes every animal in העמדה והערכה, even one blemished from the outset.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the תנא of the school of לוי. For the school of לוי taught: all animals were included in standing and valuation, even an animal blemished from the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים are the תנא דבי לוי. That תנא holds that every animal needs העמדה והערכה, even one that was blemished before it was consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a בעל מום מעיקרו needs to be stood up and valued, then once it dies it can never be redeemed. So it must be buried. This explains why the חכמים make no exception.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the school of לוי
Standing the animal before the כהן and having it valued
An animal blemished before it was consecrated

phrases.english: It is the tanna of the school of Levi,
as the school of Levi taught:
All were included in standing and valuation,
even one blemished from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי הוּא, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are the תנא דבי לוי, who requires העמדה והערכה even for an animal blemished from the outset.

steps.title: The school of לוי includes even wild animals and birds
steps.stepSummary: In his own collection, לוי taught that even a חיה and even a bird are included in העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, the school of לוי taught in his collection of ברייתות: even an undomesticated animal, even a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from לוי's collection. It shows how far his view goes: even a חיה or a bird needs העמדה והערכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חיה and a bird can never be brought on the altar, yet לוי still includes them. This shows that he reads the requirement as covering every consecrated animal with no limits. That sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His own collection of ברייתות
An undomesticated animal
A bird

phrases.english: And similarly the school of Levi taught in his collection of baraitot:
Even an undomesticated animal, even a bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further teaching that shows how broad the view in step 27 is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to לוי, even a חיה and a bird require העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: But the verse says 'אותה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges לוי from the limiting word 'אותה' in the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written 'it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks לוי's view. The verse says 'אותה' ('it'), and that word is meant to exclude some case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 we learned that 'אותה' limits העמדה והערכה and leaves an animal blemished from the outset outside it. לוי includes everything, so the word 'אותה' seems to exclude nothing in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written?
'It', a word that limits

phrases.english: But isn't it written 'it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad view of steps 27 and 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the תנא דבי לוי that every animal needs העמדה והערכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'אותה' limits the law, so it must exclude something. לוי excludes nothing.

steps.title: The גמרא admits the difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that 'אותה' remains a difficulty for the school of לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It' is difficult according to the תנא דבי לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer the challenge. It admits that 'אותה' is a real problem for לוי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The identification of the חכמים with לוי still stands, but his view has an unanswered difficulty. 'קשיא' here means the question is left open. It does not mean the view is completely rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: It remains a difficulty

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end of a line like this does not mean לוי's view is thrown out. It means the גמרא has no answer to this question.

phrases.english: 'It' is difficult according to the tanna of the school of Levi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the challenge of step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The view of the תנא דבי לוי has no answer to the word 'אותה'.

steps.title: What do the רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן who disagree with רבי שמעון also accept 'אותה', so that an animal blemished from the outset may be redeemed after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Rabbis who disagree with רבי שמעון, what do they hold? Is it so that if they died they may be redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'אותה' is difficult for לוי, the גמרא asks about the regular רבנן who argue with רבי שמעון. Do they agree that an animal blemished before consecration can be redeemed after it dies?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן also read 'אותה' as excluding a בעל מום מעיקרו, then they would agree with our משנה. That would cause a problem for רב, which the גמרא raises next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, meaning the majority
Who disagree
They may be redeemed

phrases.english: But the Rabbis who disagree
with Rabbi Shimon, what do they hold?
Is it indeed so that if they died they may be redeemed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the difficulty of step 30 and asks how it affects the Rabbis' view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Rabbis who argue with רבי שמעון agree that an animal blemished from the outset may be redeemed after death.

steps.title: If so, why did רב attribute the משנה to רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge: if the רבנן agree, why did רב say our משנה follows only רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב. The full challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the רבנן allow a בעל מום מעיקרו to be redeemed after death, then our משנה fits everyone. Then רב had no need to say it follows רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: If so

phrases.english: If so,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what follows if the answer to step 31 is 'yes', and challenges רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement in step 21 that our משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Rabbis also accept the exclusion from 'אותה', the משנה fits them too. So there is no reason to limit it to רבי שמעון.
